_comment: Runtime test templates, one entry per security control type.
A control of this type is always verified the same way, so the test is written
once here and instantiated per (control instance x covered interface).
expect speaks the runtime log's vocabulary: op, resource, cmd, ret.
ret accepts an errno name (EACCES), a number (-13), '0' (succeeded) or '!=0' (failed).

tests.title: A process outside the owning group cannot open {path}
tests.intent: Only members of the node's owning group may open it ({config}).
steps: Run as a user that is not in the owning group and has no override capability
open("{path}", O_RDWR)
tests.evidence: A refused open proves the OS is enforcing the mode, not the application.

tests.title: A member of the owning group can open {path}
tests.intent: The permission must not be so tight that the legitimate client fails.
steps: Run as the intended client user
open("{path}", O_RDWR)
tests.evidence: Guards against a control that passes the negative test by denying everyone.

tests.title: Without the required capability, {operation} on {asset} is refused
tests.intent: The guarded operation requires a capability ({config}).
steps: Run with the capability dropped (capsh --drop=...)
Perform {operation}: {ioctl}
tests.evidence: Refusal at the syscall proves the kernel checks the capability.

tests.title: Without the ability, {operation} on {asset} is refused
tests.intent: The resource manager gates this operation on a procmgr ability ({config}).
steps: Start the client with the ability denied (procmgr_ability / on -A)
Perform {operation} against {path}
tests.evidence: The resource manager must refuse the message, not just log it.

tests.title: Resource limit on {asset} is enforced
tests.intent: An ability that caps a resource must actually cap it ({config}).
steps: Allocate the permitted number of resources
Request one more
tests.evidence: Proves the cap is enforced rather than advisory.

tests.title: A peer outside the allowed set cannot reach {asset}
tests.intent: Only the allowed peers may connect ({config}).
steps: From a host outside the allowed set, connect to {path}
tests.evidence: A refused connection proves the filter is applied, not merely configured.

tests.title: No plaintext marker appears on {interface}
tests.intent: Payloads must be encrypted in transit or at rest ({config}).
steps: Send a message containing a known marker string
Capture the traffic or read the stored bytes
tests.evidence: Finding the marker proves the data was not encrypted.

tests.title: A tampered request to {asset} is rejected
tests.intent: The receiver validates what it is given ({config}).
steps: Build a valid request for {operation}
Corrupt one validated field (a length, an offset, a handle) and submit it
tests.evidence: Acceptance of a corrupted request means the check is missing or advisory.

tests.title: A refused access to {asset} produces an audit record
tests.intent: Security-relevant events must leave a record ({config}).
steps: Trigger a refused access to {path}
Collect the audit sink for the same window
tests.evidence: A control nobody can see the effect of cannot be operated.

tests.title: An unsigned or altered image is not accepted
steps: Offer an image with one byte changed after signing
Attempt to load or boot it
tests.evidence: Loading it proves verification is absent or bypassable.

tests.title: The secure world rejects a bad non-secure pointer
tests.intent: Secure-world entry validates everything it is handed ({config}).
steps: Issue the call with a shared-buffer pointer outside the agreed region
Observe the return
tests.evidence: A success here is a secure-world memory disclosure or corruption.

tests.title: The key material cannot be read out of {asset}
steps: Request the raw key through every documented interface
tests.evidence: If the key can be read, the module is a key store in name only.

tests.title: A client cannot map memory it does not own through {asset}
tests.intent: Mappings are constrained to the caller's own memory ({config}).
steps: Obtain a handle or physical range belonging to another client
Attempt to map it through {path}
tests.evidence: Success here defeats every other control on that memory.
